title: Films with Duke and Harry James; Belle of the Nineties
summary: He names Check and Double Check and the Mae West picture and some James films, remembering little.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: How about the films that you have been in?
The who?
The films.
With Harry James.
Oh, with Harry James -- I did one with Harry James and I did one with Duke, naturally. The first one was with Duke with the Amos and Andy picture.
Check and Doublecheck?

Yeah, Check and Doublecheck. We did that, and then we did one with Mae West, The Belle of the Night, that picture. I don't know what else we did with Duke, but I know with Harry, we did something with -- oh, what's this fellow's name -- a singer ...
Perry Como.
Yeah, Perry Como. And the other fellow, the other singer, I can't remember. But I know I did two or three pictures with Harry.
Uh huh. But the first one you made was with Duke, Check and Doublecheck.
No, that was the Amos and Andy.
Yeah. What do you remember about doing that picture?
Well, there is really nothing I could remember about the picture. No, I can't remember nothing about that.

In his book, "Jazz In the Movies", by David Meeker, they have a listing of Belle of the Nineties and there is a picture from it, and you're in the picture; I guess it was probably taken on the set, and it said it was at Paramount Studios in 1934. And it says it's one of the classic Mae West vehicles in which she portrays a tough 19th Century showgirl in love with a young boxer. Duke Ellington was all and sometimes part of his orchestra, provides the backing off and on screen for the songs, When A St. Louis Woman Goes Down to New Orleans, Memphis Blues, My Old Flame, and Troubled Waters. Part of Scott Joplin's Maple Leaf Rag is used for the underscore. Musicians involved are Barney Bigard, Johnny Hodges, Otto Hardwick, Harry Carney, Sam Nanton, Juan Tizol, Lawrence Brown, Freddie Jenkins, Cootie Williams, Arthur Whetsol, Wallman Braud, Wetzol, Fred Guy, Sonny Greer and Ellington. And here's the picture.
Uh huh. That was his name -- the saxophone player with Count Basie. His name didn't get in the listing. Marshal Royal, whose name doesn't get into the listing.
He was what? Instead of Toby?
Yeah, I guess so.
Yeah, because Johnny's there. Does that bring back any memories of making the picture?
The picture with Mae West, Juan.
Oh, with Mae West? Well, there was nothing that happened that I knew what happened with a Mae West picture.
